reference_use.conclusion: The snapshot (project d8d46c95, Mathlib 25730c7c) contains the frozen Ch06 Contract, a byte-identical Submission with no Submission.* declarations, and the README. The DAG contains only root, so the 12 bare child names are unreserved. All 12 conjuncts are `def … : Prop` in namespace GMT.Ch06. In a scratch build of the frozen project, every child statement elaborates in the comparator's child scope, `exact Submission.<name>` resolves for all 12 children, and the 12-way assembly typechecks against `type_of% GMT.Ch06.main_theorem`. FedererFlemingCompactness follows from its three declared siblings and the parent from the other 11 children, with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The contract's `IsLipschitzPushforward` supplies only an `IsRectifiableTriple` representation (θ′ > 0 real, integrable on compacts), confirming the v2 defect. The repaired deformation A3 uses only that. Its σ-finiteness step is kernel-checked as `v3_sigmaFinite_restrict` (via Mathlib `Measure.sigmaFinite_of_countable`, `mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral₀`, `Measure.restrict_restrict`, `ae_restrict_mem₀`), and its tangent-space step as `v3_weightedTangent_congr`, against the actual SimonGMT `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt`/`blowUpMap` definitions (via `LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le`, `Measure.restrict_congr_set`, `ae_restrict_iff'₀`; μHE[d] is a scalar multiple of μH[d]), both with standard axioms only. Mathlib provides Radon–Nikodym-type uniqueness (`ae_eq_of_forall_setIntegral_eq_of_sigmaFinite`, `Integrable.ae_eq_of_forall_setIntegral_eq`). SimonGMT provides `nVectorPushforward_simple`, `covectorEuclideanNorm` and `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`. Simon Ch. 1 gives 1.12 (μ⌞Y is Borel regular for measurable Y of finite measure), 1.15(2) (inner regularity) and 2.6 (H^m is Borel regular), as cited. There is no Mathlib match for co-area or for Besicovitch–Federer/purely unrectifiable; these are cited from Simon Ch. 3, as SimonGMT omits them. These checks do not certify the analytic proofs.

rationale:
The selected root `GMT.Ch06.main_theorem` is literally the conjunction of the 12 frozen headline Props of Simon Ch. 6 (2.15, 2.34, 3.9, 3.11, §4 slicing, 5.3, 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 7.2, 8.1, 8.2). The published chapter proves them as separate results that feed one another: deformation is used by 6.1, 6.2, 6.3 and 7.2; slicing by 5.3, 6.2, 6.3, 7.2 and 8.2; 8.2 by 6.3 and 3.11. Hence one child per conjunct (12, the maximum); each lean_statement is exactly the conjunct's Prop name, and the parent proof is the 12-tuple ⟨h1,…,h12⟩.

This is decomposition attempt 3. The v2 audit accepted the split, all 12 child statements, the dependencies and 11 of the 12 child proofs. Its single required change concerned deformation A3, which justified σ-finiteness of λ := H^k⌞(M ∪ M′) by “θ, θ′ ≥ 1”, although the representation X = τ(M′,θ′,ξ′) delivered by `IsLipschitzPushforward` only satisfies `IsRectifiableTriple` (θ′ > 0 real and integrable on compact sets). The repair follows the required change exactly. A3 is now split into (I) steps (a)–(g), unchanged in substance (g_#X equals the 3.6 formula S), and (II) steps (II.1)–(II.7) (g_#X is integer multiplicity):
- (II.1) lists precisely what `IsLipschitzPushforward X g S̃` provides, stating explicitly that θ′ need not be integer valued or ≥ 1.
- (II.3) The vector measures θξH^k⌞M and θ′ξ′H^k⌞M′ agree on bounded Borel sets (test forms φdx^γ, mollification, compact approximation, Dynkin's theorem).
- (II.4) σ-finiteness: K_j := B̄_j(0) and A′_{j,r} := M′ ∩ K_j ∩ {θ′ ≥ 1/r} with H^k(A′_{j,r}) ≤ r∫_{M′∩K_j}θ′ dH^k < ∞ (Markov), likewise for (M,θ); positivity of θ, θ′ gives M ∪ M′ = ⋃_{j,r}(A_{j,r} ∪ A′_{j,r}).
- (II.5) Radon–Nikodym uniqueness with respect to λ; Borel versions of the densities come from σ-finiteness and Borel regularity (Simon Ch. 1, 1.12, 1.15(2), 2.6).
- (II.6) Carriers H^k(M Δ M′) = 0, multiplicities θ = θ′ and orientations ξ = ξ′ hold H^k-a.e. on M ∩ M′.
- (II.7) The weighted tangent spaces coincide (checked against the Lean definition through `blowUpMap`), so do the differentials on them and the pushed-forward k-vectors. Hence S̃ = S, and g_#X is integer multiplicity.
The unsupported assertion θ′ ≥ 1 is removed, and no frozen contract is strengthened.

Further changes harden the text without changing any argument:
- deformation now states its own notation (it previously referred to conventions that appear only in another child). Its header describes the details supplied beyond the printed text instead of carrying a changelog. Symbols in A3 were renamed to avoid clashes (Ξ, κ, Γ, S̃, B_R(0), K_c, labels (II.x)), and a k = 0 remark was added after (g).
- integrality_weak_limits (P3) now spells out the identification of the sibling push-forward with the smooth push-forward, using only θ′ > 0 and local integrability, and defines the cut-off ζ.
- The patching lemmas of integrality_weak_limits (P4)(i) and boundary_rectifiability (P5)(i) now say why Radon–Nikodym uniqueness applies: θ_i ∈ {1,2,…} is locally integrable, so H^k⌞(M_i ∪ M_{i′}) is locally finite and hence σ-finite. The second index is renamed i′ to avoid a clash with the degree k.
The other nine children are byte-identical to v2.

subproblems.title: Compactness under local mass bounds (Simon 2.15)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and every sequence T_q ∈ D_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) with sup_q M_W(T_q) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContainedOpen W U), there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and T₀ ∈ D_n(U) such that T_{φ(q)} ⇀ T₀ weakly in U and, for every continuous compactly supported n-form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ U and all measure representations (μ_q, v_q) of T_{φ(q)} and (μ₀, v₀) of T₀ (IsMeasureRepresentation), ∫ v_q(x)(ω(x)) dμ_q → ∫ v₀(x)(ω(x)) dμ₀.
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, Lemma 2.15 (p. 137) together with the paragraph printed immediately before it (“We also observe that if sup_q M_W(T_q) < ∞ for each open W ⊂⊂ U then by 2.7 the distribution convergence 2.13 is equivalent to weak convergence with respect to continuous forms with compact support ..., and hence by applying the standard Banach–Alaoglu theorem (in the Banach spaces M_n(W) = {T ∈ D_n(W) : M_W(T) < ∞}, W ⊂⊂ U) we deduce 2.15”). The printed argument is: uniform local mass bounds + separability give a weakly convergent subsequence (Banach–Alaoglu / diagonal argument), and the integral representation (2.7) turns convergence on smooth forms into convergence on continuous compactly supported forms. Below the printed argument is written out in numbered steps for the exact Lean statement (in which the conclusion about continuous forms is required for every measure representation in the sense of `IsMeasureRepresentation`). No erratum applies.

Conventions. ℝ^P = `Eucl P`, e_1,…,e_P the standard basis. D^n(U) = `TestFormOn U n` (smooth n-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport ⊆ U), D_n(U) = `GeometricCurrentOn U n`. For an n-covector α let |α| := `covectorEuclideanNorm α` = (Σ_{β∈I(n,P)} α(e_β)²)^{1/2} (I(n,P) = strictly increasing multi-indices, e_β = (e_{β_1},…,e_{β_n})), and for a form ω let ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|. For an n-vector w ∈ `NVector (Eucl P) n` (a continuous linear functional on n-covectors) put w^β := w(dx^β), where dx^β = dx^{β_1}∧⋯∧dx^{β_n}, and |w| := (Σ_β (w^β)²)^{1/2}.
Fact A (coordinates). Every n-covector satisfies α = Σ_β α(e_β) dx^β (an alternating n-linear map is determined by its values on increasing tuples of basis vectors, and dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}). Hence w(α) = Σ_β α(e_β) w^β and, by Cauchy–Schwarz, |w(α)| ≤ |α|·|w|.

Proof.

1. (Exhaustion.) For i ≥ 1 let W_i := {x ∈ U : |x| < i and B̄_{1/i}(x) ⊆ U} (this avoids any convention for dist(x, ∅); if U = ℝ^P it is just the open ball of radius i). Each W_i is open; if x ∈ closure(W_i) then |x| ≤ i and B_{1/i}(x) ⊆ U (every y with |y−x| < 1/i satisfies |y − x_k| < 1/i for points x_k ∈ W_i close to x), so closure(W_i) is closed and bounded, hence compact, and closure(W_i) ⊆ W_{i+1} ⊆ U (B̄_{1/(i+1)}(x) ⊆ B_{1/i}(x)). Thus `CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U`; the W_i increase and ⋃_i W_i = U (U is open). Every compact K ⊆ U is contained in some W_i (open cover of K by an increasing sequence). Put C_i := sup_q M_{W_i}(T_q) < ∞ (hypothesis).

2. (Basic mass estimate.) If T ∈ D_n(U), W is any set and ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, then |T(ω)| ≤ M_W(T)·‖ω‖. Indeed ‖ω‖ < ∞ (ω continuous with compact support). If ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0 and T(ω) = 0. Otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ lies in `massAdmissibleOn U n W`, so ENNReal.ofReal(±T(ω)/‖ω‖) ≤ M_W(T) by `GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn`, which gives the claim (trivial if M_W(T) = ∞).

3. (Countable dense families.) Fix i. The set D_i := {ω ∈ D^n(U) : tsupport ω ⊆ W_i} is a subset of the separable metric space C(closure W_i ; Λ^n(ℝ^P)) with the sup norm built from |·| (continuous functions on a compact metric space with values in a finite-dimensional space form a separable Banach space), hence D_i is separable for ‖·‖. Choose a countable E_i ⊆ D_i which is ‖·‖-dense in D_i and put E := ⋃_i E_i, enumerated as η_1, η_2, … .

4. (Diagonal subsequence; Banach–Alaoglu step.) For η ∈ E_i, Step 2 gives |T_q(η)| ≤ C_i‖η‖ for all q, so (T_q(η_k))_q is a bounded real sequence for every k. By Bolzano–Weierstrass and Cantor's diagonal procedure there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that lim_q T_{φ(q)}(η_k) exists for every k.

5. (Convergence on every test form.) Let ω ∈ D^n(U). tsupport ω is compact and ⊆ U, so ω ∈ D_i for some i. Given ε > 0 pick η ∈ E_i with ‖ω − η‖ < ε; ω − η ∈ D_i. For all q, q′, by Step 2,
|T_{φ(q)}(ω) − T_{φ(q′)}(ω)| ≤ |T_{φ(q)}(ω−η)| + |T_{φ(q)}(η) − T_{φ(q′)}(η)| + |T_{φ(q′)}(η−ω)| ≤ 2C_iε + |T_{φ(q)}(η) − T_{φ(q′)}(η)|.
Hence (T_{φ(q)}(ω))_q is Cauchy; define T₀(ω) := lim_q T_{φ(q)}(ω).

6. (T₀ ∈ D_n(U) and T_{φ(q)} ⇀ T₀.) T₀ is linear as a pointwise limit of linear maps. Continuity: let ω_j → 0 in the sense of `TestFormOnConverges` (tsupports in one compact K ⊆ U, every iterated derivative → 0 uniformly on K). Choose i with K ⊆ W_i. By Step 2, |T_{φ(q)}(ω_j)| ≤ C_i‖ω_j‖ for all q, hence |T₀(ω_j)| ≤ C_i‖ω_j‖. Since ω_j → 0 uniformly on K and vanishes off K, and |α| ≤ (#I(n,P))^{1/2}·max_β|α(e_β)| ≤ (#I(n,P))^{1/2}·‖α‖_op, we get ‖ω_j‖ → 0, so T₀(ω_j) → 0. Thus T₀ is a `GeometricCurrentOn U n`, and `WeaklyConvergesOn (fun q => T (φ q)) T₀` holds by construction. By lower semicontinuity of mass (Simon 2.14; `WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf`), for every W ⊂⊂ U: M_W(T₀) ≤ liminf_q M_W(T_{φ(q)}) ≤ sup_q M_W(T_q) < ∞; in particular M_{W_i}(T₀) ≤ C_i.

7. (Representation lemma; this is the content of “by 2.7” in the printed text.) Let T ∈ D_n(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U and let (μ, v) satisfy `IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v`, i.e. for every ω ∈ D^n(U) the function x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and T(ω) = ∫ v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x).
 (a) For every compact K ⊆ U, x ↦ |v(x)| is μ-integrable on K and each v^β is a.e.-strongly measurable on K. Proof: take χ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K, tsupport χ ⊆ U. For each β the form ω_β := χ·dx^β (constant covector times χ) lies in D^n(U) and v(x)(ω_β(x)) = χ(x)v^β(x) (Fact A). By hypothesis χv^β is μ-integrable, hence v^β is μ-integrable on K, and |v| ≤ Σ_β|v^β| is μ-integrable on K.
 (b) Let ω be a continuous n-form with compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ W where W is open with closure(W) compact ⊆ U. Then x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and |∫ v(ω) dμ| ≤ M_W(T)‖ω‖. Proof: measurability and integrability follow from v(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_β ω(x)(e_β)v^β(x) and |v(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖|v|1_{tsupport ω} with (a). Choose δ > 0 such that the closed δ-neighbourhood K′ of tsupport ω lies in W. Let ϕ be a smooth mollifier (ϕ ≥ 0, ∫ϕ = 1, spt ϕ ⊆ B_1(0)), ϕ_ε(x) = ε^{−P}ϕ(x/ε), and for 0 < ε < δ let ω_ε := ϕ_ε * ω (convolution of each coefficient function x ↦ ω(x)(e_β), equivalently of the covector-valued function). Then ω_ε is smooth, tsupport ω_ε ⊆ K′ ⊆ W (so ω_ε ∈ D^n(U)), |ω_ε(x)| ≤ ∫|ω(x−y)|ϕ_ε(y)dy ≤ ‖ω‖ (convexity of the Euclidean norm on coefficient vectors), and ω_ε → ω uniformly as ε ↓ 0 (uniform continuity of ω). By Step 2, |∫ v(ω_ε)dμ| = |T(ω_ε)| ≤ M_W(T)‖ω‖. By dominated convergence (dominating function ‖ω‖·|v|·1_{K′}, integrable by (a)), ∫v(ω_ε)dμ → ∫v(ω)dμ. Hence |∫ v(ω)dμ| ≤ M_W(T)‖ω‖.
 The same mollification shows: every such ω is a uniform limit of test forms ω_ε ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport ω_ε ⊆ W.

8. (Convergence on continuous compactly supported forms.) Let ω : ℝ^P → Λ^n(ℝ^P) be continuous with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U, and let (μ_q, v_q), (μ₀, v₀) be representations of T_{φ(q)} and T₀. Choose i with tsupport ω ⊆ W_i and put W := W_{i+1} (so closure(W_i) ⊆ W ⊂⊂ U). Let ε > 0. By Step 7 there is a test form η ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W and ‖ω − η‖ ≤ ε; ω − η is continuous with compact tsupport ⊆ W. Since all integrands are integrable (Step 7(b)) the integrals are linear, and by Step 7(b) together with T_{φ(q)}(η) = ∫v_q(η)dμ_q and T₀(η) = ∫v₀(η)dμ₀:
|∫v_q(ω)dμ_q − ∫v₀(ω)dμ₀| ≤ |∫v_q(ω−η)dμ_q| + |T_{φ(q)}(η) − T₀(η)| + |∫v₀(η−ω)dμ₀| ≤ C_{i+1}ε + |T_{φ(q)}(η) − T₀(η)| + M_W(T₀)ε.
Here M_W(T_{φ(q)}) ≤ C_{i+1} and M_W(T₀) ≤ C_{i+1} (Step 6). Since T_{φ(q)}(η) → T₀(η), limsup_q |∫v_q(ω)dμ_q − ∫v₀(ω)dμ₀| ≤ 2C_{i+1}ε; ε being arbitrary, ∫ v_q(ω) dμ_q → ∫ v₀(ω) dμ₀.

9. (Degenerate cases.) If U = ∅ every test form and every ω with tsupport ω ⊆ ∅ is 0; then any strictly increasing φ and T₀ := 0 satisfy all conclusions (all integrals vanish). Steps 1–8 also cover this case formally. This proves `CompactnessUnderMassBounds`.
proof_key_steps: Exhaust U by open W_i ⊂⊂ U with closure W_i ⊆ W_{i+1}; C_i := sup_q M_{W_i}(T_q) < ∞.
Mass estimate |T(ω)| ≤ M_W(T)‖ω‖ for tsupport ω ⊆ W (±ω/‖ω‖ is mass-admissible).
Choose countable sup-norm-dense families E_i of test forms supported in W_i (separability).
Diagonal (Bolzano–Weierstrass / Banach–Alaoglu) subsequence converging on all of E = ⋃E_i.
Cauchy argument extends convergence to every test form; define T₀ as the limit.
T₀ is linear and sequentially continuous (|T₀(ω)| ≤ C_i‖ω‖), and M_W(T₀) ≤ sup_q M_W(T_q) by 2.14.
Any IsMeasureRepresentation (μ,v) has |v| locally μ-integrable and |∫v(ω)dμ| ≤ M_W(T)‖ω‖ for continuous ω (mollification + dominated convergence).
Approximate continuous ω uniformly by test forms supported in W_{i+1} to get convergence of ∫v_q(ω)dμ_q to ∫v₀(ω)dμ₀.

subproblems.title: Constancy theorem (Simon 2.34)
subproblems.statement: For every m ∈ ℕ, every open connected U ⊆ ℝ^{m+1} and every T ∈ D_{m+1}(U) with ∂T = 0 there is c ∈ ℝ such that T(ω) = c·∫_U ω(x)(e_1,…,e_{m+1}) dL^{m+1}(x) for every test form ω ∈ D^{m+1}(U).
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, Theorem 2.34 and its printed proof (p. 142–143); book n = m + 1. The printed proof is copied below in numbered form, with the details it leaves implicit filled in. Erratum applied: the printed display (1) is garbled; it must read T(a_ε dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ) = ∫ a θ^{(ε)} dLⁿ for a ∈ L¹(B_{R−ε}(x₀)) (the left side involves the mollified function a_ε = ϕ_ε * a, as the preceding sentence of the proof defines F(a) = T(a_ε dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ)).

Setting. n = m + 1 ≥ 1, U ⊆ ℝⁿ open and connected (nonempty), T ∈ D_n(U) = `GeometricCurrentOn U n`, ∂T = `T.boundary` = 0. Lⁿ = `volume` on `Eucl n` (Lebesgue measure). dx = dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ denotes the n-covector v ↦ det[v₁ … v_n], so dx(e₁,…,e_n) = 1.

Proof.

1. (Reduction to a distribution.) Every n-covector α on ℝⁿ equals α(e₁,…,e_n)·dx (an alternating n-linear form on an n-dimensional space is a multiple of the determinant). Hence every ω ∈ D^n(U) equals a_ω dx with a_ω(x) := ω(x)(e₁,…,e_n), a_ω ∈ C_c^∞(U), and conversely a dx ∈ D^n(U) for every a ∈ C_c^∞(U). Define u(a) := T(a dx) for a ∈ C_c^∞(U). u is linear, and if a_k → a in C_c^∞(U) (supports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U, all derivatives converging uniformly) then a_k dx → a dx in D^n(U) (`TestFormOnConverges`), so u(a_k) → u(a). The theorem is equivalent to: there is c ∈ ℝ with u(a) = c ∫ a dLⁿ for all a ∈ C_c^∞(U) (then T(ω) = u(a_ω) = c∫_U ω(x)(e₁,…,e_n) dLⁿ(x), since a_ω vanishes off U).

2. (∂T = 0 gives zero derivatives.) Let a ∈ C_c^∞(U), j ∈ {1,…,n}, and ω_j := (−1)^{j−1} a dx¹∧⋯∧dx^{j−1}∧dx^{j+1}∧⋯∧dxⁿ ∈ D^{n−1}(U). By the formula for the exterior derivative (Simon 1.11; `exteriorDerivative_apply`), dω_j = (D_j a) dx. Hence u(D_j a) = T(dω_j) = ∂T(ω_j) = 0.

3. (Mollified representation on a ball — printed (1).) Fix x₀ ∈ U and R > 0 with the closed ball B̄_R(x₀) ⊆ U. Let ϕ ∈ C_c^∞(B_1(0)), ϕ ≥ 0, ϕ even, ∫ϕ = 1, ϕ_ε(x) := ε^{−n}ϕ(x/ε). Fix 0 < ε < R/2. For a ∈ L¹(B_{R−ε}(x₀)) (extended by 0) let a_ε := ϕ_ε * a; then a_ε ∈ C^∞ with spt a_ε ⊆ B̄_R(x₀), so a_ε ∈ C_c^∞(U). Define F(a) := u(a_ε). F is linear on L¹(B_{R−ε}(x₀)) and sequentially continuous: if a_k → a in L¹ then D^β(a_k)_ε = (D^βϕ_ε) * a_k → (D^βϕ_ε) * a = D^β a_ε uniformly for every multi-index β, with all supports in B̄_R(x₀), so u((a_k)_ε) → u(a_ε) by Step 1. A sequentially continuous linear functional on a normed space is bounded, so by the Riesz representation (L¹)* = L^∞ there is θ_ε ∈ L^∞(B_{R−ε}(x₀)) with
(1) u(a_ε) = ∫ a θ_ε dLⁿ for all a ∈ L¹(B_{R−ε}(x₀)).

4. (θ_ε is constant — printed (2).) For a ∈ C_c^∞(B_{R−ε}(x₀)) we have (D_j a)_ε = D_j(a_ε) and a_ε ∈ C_c^∞(U), so by (1) and Step 2:
(2) ∫ (D_j a) θ_ε dLⁿ = u((D_j a)_ε) = u(D_j(a_ε)) = 0, j = 1,…,n.
Thus θ_ε has zero distributional gradient on the ball B := B_{R−ε}(x₀). For 0 < σ < R − ε and x ∈ B_{R−ε−σ}(x₀), the function a(y) := ϕ_σ(x − y) lies in C_c^∞(B) and D_{y_j}a(y) = −(D_jϕ_σ)(x − y); hence D_j(ϕ_σ * θ_ε)(x) = ∫(D_jϕ_σ)(x−y)θ_ε(y)dy = −∫(D_j a)θ_ε dLⁿ = 0 by (2). So ϕ_σ * θ_ε is smooth with zero gradient on the connected ball B_{R−ε−σ}(x₀), hence constant there. Since ϕ_σ * θ_ε → θ_ε in L¹_loc(B) as σ ↓ 0, θ_ε equals a constant c_ε Lⁿ-a.e. on B. Consequently u(a_ε) = c_ε ∫ a dLⁿ for all a ∈ L¹(B_{R−ε}(x₀)).

5. (Letting ε ↓ 0.) Let r := R/2 and b ∈ C_c^∞(B_r(x₀)). For 0 < ε < R/2, b ∈ L¹(B_{R−ε}(x₀)), so u(b_ε) = c_ε∫b. As ε ↓ 0, b_ε → b in C_c^∞(U) (supports in B̄_R(x₀), all derivatives converge uniformly), so u(b_ε) → u(b). Fix b₀ ∈ C_c^∞(B_r(x₀)) with ∫b₀ = 1; then c_ε = u((b₀)_ε) → u(b₀) =: c(x₀). Hence for every b ∈ C_c^∞(B_r(x₀)): u(b) = lim_ε c_ε∫b = c(x₀)∫b. Write r(x₀) := r. (This is the printed conclusion “T = c_{x₀}[[B_{R−ε}(x₀)]] on each ball”.)

6. (The constant is global.) If B_{r(x₀)}(x₀) ∩ B_{r(x₁)}(x₁) ≠ ∅, choose b ∈ C_c^∞ of this (open, nonempty) intersection with ∫b = 1; Step 5 for both balls gives c(x₀) = u(b) = c(x₁). In particular, for y ∈ B_{r(x₀)}(x₀) the balls around y and x₀ both contain y, so c(y) = c(x₀): the function c : U → ℝ is locally constant. U is connected, so c is constant, c ≡ c.

7. (Partition of unity.) Let a ∈ C_c^∞(U). Cover the compact spt a by finitely many balls B_k := B_{r(x_k)}(x_k), k = 1,…,K, and choose χ_k ∈ C_c^∞(B_k) with Σ_k χ_k = 1 on spt a (smooth partition of unity). Then by Step 5 and Step 6, u(a) = Σ_k u(χ_k a) = Σ_k c∫χ_k a dLⁿ = c∫a dLⁿ. By Step 1, T(ω) = c ∫_U ω(x)(e₁,…,e_n) dLⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ D^n(U), which is `ConstancyTheorem`.
proof_key_steps: Write ω = a_ω dx¹∧⋯∧dxⁿ and set u(a) := T(a dx), a continuous linear functional on C_c^∞(U).
∂T = 0 gives u(D_j a) = 0 for all j (dω_j = D_j a dx).
On a ball, F(a) := u(ϕ_ε*a) is a bounded functional on L¹, so u(a_ε) = ∫aθ_ε with θ_ε ∈ L^∞ (printed (1), corrected).
θ_ε has zero distributional gradient, hence is a.e. a constant c_ε (printed (2) + mollification).
Letting ε ↓ 0 gives u(b) = c(x₀)∫b for b supported in a smaller ball.
Overlapping balls give equal constants; connectedness makes c constant on U.
Partition of unity gives T(ω) = c∫_U ω(e₁,…,e_n) dLⁿ.

subproblems.title: Lipschitz push-forward of integer multiplicity currents (Simon 3.9)
subproblems.statement: For all P, Q, n, open U ⊆ ℝ^P and V ⊆ ℝ^Q, every integer multiplicity T ∈ D_n(U) and every f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q that is locally Lipschitz on U with f(U) ⊆ V and f⁻¹(K) ∩ spt T compact for every compact K ⊆ V, there is S ∈ D_n(V) such that S = f_#T in the sense of (3.6) (IsLipschitzPushforward T f S, i.e. S(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)), L(x)_#ξ(x)⟩dHⁿ for a representation T = τ(M,θ,ξ) and linear maps L(x) giving the directional derivatives of f along the weighted approximate tangent space), and S is integer multiplicity.
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, 3.3–3.9 (pp. 146–148): the definition (3.6) of f_#T for an integer multiplicity T = τ(M,θ,ξ) and a Lipschitz f with f|spt T proper, the computations 3.4–3.5, the area-formula rewriting 3.6–3.8 and the conclusion Lemma 3.9 (f_#T = τ(f(M), N, ζ)). The printed argument is copied below in numbered form; the points it leaves implicit for the exact Lean statement (the choice of the linear maps L(x) required by `IsLipschitzPushforward`, the integrability that makes S a current, the printed assertion that for Hⁿ-a.e. y the approximate tangent space T_y(f(M)) exists and is the image d^Mf_x(T_xM) for every x ∈ f⁻¹(y) ∩ M₊ (needed for 3.7), and the verification of every field of `IsRectifiableTriple`) are filled in. No erratum applies (the printed “Hence (a) gives” refers to 3.6). Correction of the previous draft (Step 5): the images f(A_k) of different source pieces may overlap with positive density (two sheets may project onto the same plane region), so no claim is made that one image piece has zero density at the points of another. Instead, Step 5.3 compares every piece with the whole image Y = f(M₊): the complement Y ∖ f(A_k) has zero density at almost every point of f(A_k), which gives T_yY = T_y f(A_k) = T_yN′_k there (so overlapping sheets automatically have the same pushed-forward tangent plane), and the exceptional image sets are pulled back to Hⁿ-null source sets through the area formula, so that the agreement holds for every contributing preimage at Hⁿ-almost every image point.

Setting. U ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^Q open; T ∈ D_n(U) integer multiplicity: T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω,ξ⟩dHⁿ for all ω ∈ Dⁿ(U), with `IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ` and θ(x) ∈ {1,2,…} on M; f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q locally Lipschitz on U, f(U) ⊆ V, and f⁻¹(K) ∩ spt T compact for every compact K ⊆ V. Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Notation |α|, ‖ω‖, w^β, |w| and Fact A (w(α) = Σ_β α(e_β)w^β, |w(α)| ≤ |α||w|) are as in the conventions: |α| = `covectorEuclideanNorm α`, w^β = w(dx^β).

Preliminary facts.
(P1) If τ₁,…,τ_n are orthonormal then |simpleNVector τ| = 1 (coordinates are the n×n minors det(τ_i·e_{β_j}); by Cauchy–Binet Σ_β det(τ_i·e_{β_j})² = det(τ_i·τ_j) = 1). For a linear map A, A_#(simpleNVector τ) = simpleNVector(Aτ) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`) and |A_#(simpleNVector τ)| = det(Aτ_i·Aτ_j)^{1/2} =: J_A(span τ), the Jacobian of A on span τ; it is ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ and it is 0 iff A|span τ has rank < n. Hence |⟨α, A_#ξ⟩| ≤ |α|·J_A ≤ |α|‖A‖ⁿ when ξ = ±simpleNVector τ.
(P2) Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) = 0. Proof: U ∖ spt T is the union of the open sets W (closure W compact ⊆ U) on which T vanishes; by Lindelöf countably many W_k suffice. Fix k. For φ ∈ C_c^∞(W_k) and β ∈ I(n,P), the test form φ dx^β gives 0 = T(φ dx^β) = ∫_{M} φ θ ξ^β dHⁿ. The signed measures ν_β := θξ^β Hⁿ⌞M are Radon on U (θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U, |ξ^β| ≤ |ξ| = 1 Hⁿ-a.e. on M by P1 and the orientation property). A signed Radon measure on W_k annihilating C_c^∞(W_k) vanishes on W_k, so θ|ξ| = 0 Hⁿ-a.e. on M ∩ W_k; since θ > 0 on M and |ξ| = 1 a.e. on M, Hⁿ(M ∩ W_k) = 0. Summing over k gives the claim (M ⊆ U).
(P3) (Null sets and measurability under f.) (i) If Z ⊆ U and Hⁿ(Z) = 0 then Hⁿ(f(Z)) = 0: since f is locally Lipschitz on the open set U, U is the union of countably many open balls B (closure in U) on each of which f is Lipschitz (Lindelöf), and Hⁿ(f(Z ∩ B)) ≤ (Lip f|_B)ⁿHⁿ(Z ∩ B) = 0. (ii) If A ⊆ U is Hⁿ-measurable with Hⁿ⌞A σ-finite, then f(A) is Hⁿ-measurable: by inner regularity of the Borel regular measure Hⁿ on sets of finite measure (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15: closed inner approximants, intersected with closed balls B̄_R to make them compact) A = ⋃_iC_i ∪ Z with C_i compact and Hⁿ(Z) = 0; each f(C_i) is compact (f is continuous on U) and Hⁿ(f(Z)) = 0 by (i).
(P4) (Locality of approximate tangent spaces; Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4, the proof of 1.6 “⇒”, Remark 1.5(2), and the Upper Density Theorem Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2).) Let V₀ ⊆ ℝ^Q be open and Y ⊆ V₀ Hⁿ-measurable with Hⁿ(Y ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ V₀; approximate tangent spaces T_yY (Definition 1.4) at y ∈ V₀ only involve Y ∩ B for an arbitrarily small ball B ∋ y, so Definition 1.4 and Ch. 3, 1.6 are applied to Y ∩ V₀^{(i)} for open V₀^{(i)} ⊂⊂ V₀ exhausting V₀. (a) (Subsets.) If Y′ ⊆ Y is Hⁿ-measurable, then for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ Y′ the upper density Θ*ⁿ(Hⁿ⌞(Y ∖ Y′), y) is 0 (Upper Density Theorem applied to the set (Y ∖ Y′) ∩ V₀^{(i)} of finite measure, at points of Y′ ∩ V₀^{(i)}, which lie outside it), and at every such y: T_yY exists ⇔ T_yY′ exists, and then T_yY = T_yY′. Indeed for φ ∈ C_c^0(ℝ^Q) with spt φ ⊆ B_R(0) and small λ, |∫_{η_{y,λ}(Y)}φ dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{y,λ}(Y′)}φ dHⁿ| ≤ sup|φ|·λ^{−n}Hⁿ((Y∖Y′) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0. (b) (Subsets of C¹ manifolds.) If N ⊆ ℝ^Q is an embedded n-dimensional C¹ submanifold and Y′ ⊆ N is Hⁿ-measurable, then T_yY′ exists and equals the classical tangent space T_yN for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ Y′: every y ∈ N has a ball B with N ∩ B a single C¹ graph of finite Hⁿ-measure, T_y(N ∩ B) = T_yN at every point of N ∩ B (C¹ blow-up, as in the proof of Ch. 3, 1.6 “⇒”), and (a) applies to Y′ ∩ B ⊆ N ∩ B; countably many such balls cover N. (c) (Existence.) If Y is moreover countably n-rectifiable then T_yY exists for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ Y (Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 applied to Y ∩ V₀^{(i)}).

Proof.

1. (Structure of M; Simon Ch. 3, 1.2–1.3, 1.8–1.9. These results assume ∫_{M∩K}θ < ∞ for all compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; here this holds for compact K ⊆ U, so they are applied to M ∩ U_i for open U_i ⊂⊂ U exhausting U — weighted tangent spaces at points of U_i only depend on M ∩ U_i and θ there.) M is countably n-rectifiable and Hⁿ-measurable, so M = ⋃_{j≥0} M_j (disjoint, Hⁿ-measurable) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and M_j ⊆ N_j, N_j embedded n-dimensional C¹ submanifolds of ℝ^P. Since θ ≥ 1 and θ is integrable on M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ⌞M is locally finite in U. By Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 and Remark 1.8(1), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M the weighted approximate tangent space T_xM of M with respect to θ exists (`HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x (T_xM)`), and T_xM = T_xN_j for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_j (Remark 1.8(1) identifies the weighted tangent space with the approximate tangent space of a Lusin piece of M, and P4(a),(b) below — applied to that piece intersected with M_j ⊆ N_j — identify the latter with T_xN_j a.e.). By the `orients` field, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector(τ(x)) with τ(x) an orthonormal basis of T_xM; the weighted tangent space is unique when θ(x) > 0 (`HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`).

2. (The tangential differential d^M f and the maps L(x); Simon Ch. 3 §2, p. 76.) Fix j ≥ 1 and x ∈ N_j. Writing ℝ^P = T_xN_j ⊕ (T_xN_j)^⊥, a neighbourhood of x in N_j is {x + w + g(w)} for a C¹ map g defined near 0 ∈ T_xN_j with g(0) = 0, Dg(0) = 0; Φ_x(w) := x + w + g(w) is a C¹ chart. f∘Φ_x is Lipschitz near 0. Covering N_j ∩ U by countably many such charts (Lindelöf: N_j is second countable) and using Rademacher's theorem in each chart together with the fact that C¹ charts map Lⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets, we get: for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_j the map f|N_j is differentiable at x, i.e. there is a linear map d^M f_x : T_xN_j → ℝ^Q with f(Φ_x(w)) = f(x) + d^Mf_x(w) + o(|w|). For v ∈ T_xN_j and t → 0, x + tv = Φ_x(tv) − g(tv) with |g(tv)| = o(t), so |f(x+tv) − f(Φ_x(tv))| ≤ Lip·o(t) (f is Lipschitz near x because x ∈ U and f is locally Lipschitz on U); hence t ↦ f(x + tv) is differentiable at t = 0 with derivative d^Mf_x(v), for every v ∈ T_xN_j simultaneously. Define L(x) := d^Mf_x ∘ π_{T_xM} (π = orthogonal projection) at the Hⁿ-a.e. points x ∈ M where all of the above holds and T_xM = T_xN_j, and L(x) := 0 otherwise. L is Hⁿ⌞M-measurable: the orthogonal projection onto T_xM is a continuous function of ξ(x) invariant under ξ ↦ −ξ (so it is measurable), Gram–Schmidt with measurable case distinctions gives a measurable orthonormal frame τ(x) of T_xM, and L(x)τ_i(x) = lim_{k→∞}1_{{dist(·,ℝ^P∖U) > 1/k}}(x)·k(f(x + τ_i(x)/k) − f(x)) a.e. (the cut-off keeps x + τ_i(x)/k in U, where f is continuous, so each term is measurable); thus L agrees Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. with a measurable map, which is all that is needed for the measurability of the integrands below; and for every compact K ⊆ U, Λ_K := sup_{x∈K∩M} ‖L(x)‖ < ∞ (cover K by finitely many open sets on which f is Lipschitz; ‖d^Mf_x‖ is bounded by the Lipschitz constant there). Consequently: for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, for every T_x with `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T_x` we have T_x = T_xM (uniqueness, θ(x) > 0) and `HasDerivAt (fun t => f (x + t • v)) (L x v) 0` for all v ∈ T_x. This is the third clause of `IsLipschitzPushforward`.

3. (Definition of S = f_#T, printed 3.6, and well-definedness.) For ω ∈ Dⁿ(V) set
S(ω) := ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(f(x)), L(x)_#ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) = ∫_M θ(x)·`nVectorPushforward n (L x) (ξ x)`(ω(f(x))) dHⁿ(x).
Let K := tsupport ω (compact ⊆ V) and K′ := f⁻¹(K) ∩ spt T, compact ⊆ U by hypothesis. The integrand vanishes unless f(x) ∈ K, and by (P2) Hⁿ-a.e. such x ∈ M lies in K′. On M ∩ K′ the integrand is measurable and bounded by θ(x)‖ω‖Λ_{K′}ⁿ (P1, Step 2), and θ is integrable on M ∩ K′ (`integrableOn` of the triple). So S(ω) is an absolutely convergent integral, S is linear, and if ω_k → 0 in Dⁿ(V) with tsupports in one compact K, dominated convergence (same dominating function with ‖ω_k‖ → 0) gives S(ω_k) → 0. Hence S ∈ `GeometricCurrentOn V n`, and `IsLipschitzPushforward T f S` holds with the data (M, θ, ξ, L) (the first two clauses are the given i.m. representation of T, the third is Step 2, the fourth is the definition of S).

4. (Printed 3.4–3.5: where the Jacobian vanishes and the induced orientation.) Let J^Mf(x) := |L(x)_#ξ(x)| = Jacobian of d^Mf_x on T_xM (P1) and M₊ := {x ∈ M : J^Mf(x) > 0}. On M ∖ M₊, L(x)_#ξ(x) = 0 (rank d^Mf_x < n), so S(ω) = ∫_{M₊} θ⟨ω∘f, L_#ξ⟩dHⁿ. For x ∈ M₊ put η_x := L(x)_#ξ(x)/J^Mf(x); since L(x)_#ξ(x) = ±(d^Mf_xτ₁)∧⋯∧(d^Mf_xτ_n), η_x is a unit simple n-vector orienting the n-plane d^Mf_x(T_xM) (printed 3.5: d f_{x#} ξ = J^Mf(x)·η). (This holds at every x ∈ M₊ where L(x) is defined by Step 2, not only where the orientation property holds: L(x) = d^Mf_x∘π_{T_xM} has range d^Mf_x(T_xM), so L(x)_# maps every n-vector into the one-dimensional space Λ_n(d^Mf_x(T_xM)), and a nonzero element of it, normalized, is a unit simple n-vector orienting that plane.)

5. (Printed 3.6–3.8: area formula, tangent agreement, multiplicities.)
 5.1 (Consequences of the area formula; Simon Ch. 3, 2.4–2.5.) For every Hⁿ-measurable A ⊆ M and every Hⁿ-measurable h ≥ 0 on M, ∫_A hJ^Mf dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝ^Q}Σ_{x∈A∩f⁻¹(y)}h(x) dHⁿ(y) (Simon states 2.4–2.5 for f locally Lipschitz on an open set containing M, which is the present situation; for integrable signed h split h = h⁺ − h⁻). Consequences:
  (a) If E ⊆ ℝ^Q is Hⁿ-null, then Hⁿ(M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(E)) = 0. Indeed choose a Borel Hⁿ-null E′ ⊇ E; A := M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(E′) is Hⁿ-measurable (f is continuous on U), ∫_AJ^Mf dHⁿ = ∫_{E′}#(A ∩ f⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = 0 and J^Mf > 0 on A, so Hⁿ(A) = 0.
  (b) For compact K ⊆ V let K′ := f⁻¹(K) ∩ spt T (compact ⊆ U by hypothesis). Then ∫_K Σ_{x∈M₊∩K′∩f⁻¹(y)}θ(x) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{M₊∩K′}θJ^Mf dHⁿ ≤ Λ_{K′}ⁿ∫_{M∩K′}θ dHⁿ < ∞ (P1, Step 2), and Hⁿ(f(M₊ ∩ K′)) ≤ ∫#(M₊ ∩ K′ ∩ f⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{M₊∩K′}J^Mf dHⁿ < ∞ (θ ≥ 1).
  (c) Hⁿ(f(M ∖ M₊)) ≤ ∫#((M∖M₊) ∩ f⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{M∖M₊}J^Mf dHⁿ = 0, and Hⁿ(f(M ∖ spt T)) = 0 (P2, P3(i)).
 Put Y := f(M₊). Then: Y ⊆ f(U) ⊆ V; Y is Hⁿ-measurable (P3(ii); Hⁿ⌞M is locally finite in U, so M₊ is Hⁿ-σ-finite); Y is countably n-rectifiable (M ⊆ M₀′ ∪ ⋃_jF_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀′) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz; for each of the countably many balls B of P3(i), f∘F_j restricted to F_j⁻¹(B) is Lipschitz and extends to a Lipschitz map ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q, and f(M₀′ ∩ U) is null by P3(i)); and for every compact K ⊆ V, Y ∩ K ⊆ f(M₊ ∩ K′) ∪ f(M ∖ spt T), so Hⁿ(Y ∩ K) < ∞ by (b), (c). By P4(c) (with V₀ := V), T_yY exists for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ Y.
 5.2 (Source pieces on which f is an injective C¹ immersion; Simon Ch. 2, 1.5 (C¹ approximation) and the inverse function theorem.) Fix j ≥ 1 and a C¹ chart Φ : Ω → N_j (Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Φ a C¹ diffeomorphism onto a relatively open subset of N_j contained in one of the balls B of P3(i), so f is Lipschitz on Φ(Ω)); countably many such charts cover M_j ⊆ N_j ∩ U. The map u := f∘Φ is locally Lipschitz on Ω; at every w with x := Φ(w) in the full-measure set of Step 2 (where f∘Φ_x is differentiable at 0 with derivative d^Mf_x), the chain rule applied to u = (f∘Φ_x)∘(Φ_x⁻¹∘Φ) near w gives that u is differentiable at w with Du(w) = d^Mf_x∘DΦ(w) (D(Φ_x⁻¹∘Φ)(w) = DΦ(w), whose range is T_xN_j). Shrinking the charts we may assume Φ is Lipschitz on Ω; then u is Lipschitz on Ω and extends (componentwise McShane) to a Lipschitz map ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q. By Ch. 2, 1.5 (componentwise), for each i ≥ 1 there is G_i ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ;ℝ^Q) with Lⁿ({u ≠ G_i} ∪ {Du ≠ DG_i}) < 1/i; so Ω = Z ∪ ⋃_iΩ_i with Lⁿ(Z) = 0 and Ω_i := {w : u(w) = G_i(w), u differentiable at w, Du(w) = DG_i(w)} (Lebesgue measurable). If w ∈ Ω_i and x = Φ(w) ∈ M₊ is a point of Step 2 with T_xM = T_xN_j, then DG_i(w) = d^Mf_x∘DΦ(w) has rank n (J^Mf(x) > 0), so by the inverse function theorem (local immersion theorem) w has an open neighbourhood O ⊆ Ω such that G_i|O is injective and N′ := G_i(O) is an embedded n-dimensional C¹ submanifold of ℝ^Q with T_{G_i(w′)}N′ = DG_i(w′)(ℝⁿ) for w′ ∈ O; at such points, f(x) = G_i(w) and d^Mf_x(T_xM) = d^Mf_x(DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ)) = DG_i(w)(ℝⁿ) = T_{f(x)}N′. By Lindelöf, countably many such O cover these points of Ω_i. Since Φ is locally Lipschitz, Φ maps Lⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets, and Φ⁻¹ (locally Lipschitz on Φ(Ω)) maps Hⁿ-null sets to Lⁿ-null sets. Collecting over all j, charts, i and neighbourhoods O (countably many), intersecting each piece Φ(O ∩ Ω_i) with M₊ ∩ M_j for the chart's own j, and disjointifying, we obtain pairwise disjoint Hⁿ-measurable sets A_k ⊆ M₊ (k ∈ ℕ) with Hⁿ(M₊ ∖ ⋃_kA_k) = 0, and for each k an embedded n-dimensional C¹ submanifold N′_k ⊆ ℝ^Q and an Hⁿ-null set Z⁰_k ⊆ A_k such that: f|A_k is injective (f = G_i∘Φ⁻¹ on A_k with G_i|O injective), f(A_k) ⊆ N′_k, the inverse (f|A_k)⁻¹ is the restriction to f(A_k) of the continuous map Φ∘(G_i|O)⁻¹ on N′_k, and for every x ∈ A_k ∖ Z⁰_k: T_xM exists and equals T_xN_j, the orientation property ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ(x) holds, Step 2 holds at x, and d^Mf_x(T_xM) = T_{f(x)}N′_k (Z⁰_k collects the Hⁿ-null sets where one of these fails, together with the image under Φ of the Lⁿ-null exceptional sets of the chart). Put Y_k := f(A_k) ⊆ Y ∩ N′_k (Hⁿ-measurable by P3(ii)).
 5.3 (Tangent agreement for every contributing preimage at Hⁿ-a.e. image point.) Claim: there is an Hⁿ-null set E ⊆ ℝ^Q such that for every y ∈ Y ∖ E the approximate tangent space T_yY exists and d^Mf_x(T_xM) = T_yY for every x ∈ f⁻¹(y) ∩ M₊ (in particular each such x is a point where T_xM and d^Mf_x exist). Proof.
  (i) E₁ := {y ∈ Y : T_yY does not exist} is Hⁿ-null (5.1).
  (ii) For each k apply P4(a) to Y_k ⊆ Y (V₀ := V; this uses the local finiteness of Hⁿ⌞Y proved in 5.1: the image complement Y ∖ Y_k has upper density 0 at Hⁿ-a.e. point of Y_k, whether or not other images Y_{k′} overlap Y_k), and P4(b) to Y_k ⊆ N′_k: there is an Hⁿ-null set E_{2,k} ⊆ Y_k such that T_yY = T_yY_k = T_yN′_k for every y ∈ Y_k ∖ (E₁ ∪ E_{2,k}). (On an overlap Y_k ∩ Y_{k′}, outside E₁ ∪ E_{2,k} ∪ E_{2,k′}, this gives T_yN′_k = T_yY = T_yN′_{k′}: different sheets through the same image point have the same pushed-forward tangent plane.)
  (iii) Pull back the exceptional sets through the area formula: Z_k := A_k ∩ f⁻¹(E₁ ∪ E_{2,k}) is Hⁿ-null by 5.1(a). For x ∈ A_k ∖ (Z_k ∪ Z⁰_k) and y := f(x) ∈ Y_k ∖ (E₁ ∪ E_{2,k}): d^Mf_x(T_xM) = T_yN′_k = T_yY.
  (iv) B := (M₊ ∖ ⋃_kA_k) ∪ ⋃_k(Z_k ∪ Z⁰_k) is an Hⁿ-null subset of M₊, so E := E₁ ∪ f(B) is Hⁿ-null (P3(i)). If y ∈ Y ∖ E and x ∈ f⁻¹(y) ∩ M₊, then x ∉ B (otherwise y ∈ f(B)), so x ∈ A_k ∖ (Z_k ∪ Z⁰_k) for the unique k with x ∈ A_k, and (iii) gives d^Mf_x(T_xM) = T_yY. This proves the claim.
 5.4 (Printed 3.7–3.8: the induced orientation and the multiplicity.) Enlarge E by the Hⁿ-null set f(M ∖ spt T) (5.1(c)) and, for each K = K_i of a compact exhaustion K_1 ⊆ K_2 ⊆ ⋯ of V, by the Hⁿ-null set of y ∈ K_i with Σ_{x∈M₊∩K_i′∩f⁻¹(y)}θ(x) = ∞ (5.1(b)); E stays Hⁿ-null and the claim of 5.3 still holds off E. For y ∈ Y ∖ E let F_y := f⁻¹(y) ∩ M₊. Then F_y ⊆ spt T (as y ∉ f(M ∖ spt T)), hence F_y ⊆ K_i′ for every i with y ∈ K_i, so Σ_{x∈F_y}θ(x) < ∞, and since θ ≥ 1 the fibre F_y is finite (and nonempty, as y ∈ f(M₊)). By Step 4 and 5.3, every η_x (x ∈ F_y) is a unit simple n-vector orienting the same n-plane T_yY. For a unit simple n-vector w let s(w) := w if the first nonzero coordinate w^γ (γ ∈ I(n,Q) in lexicographic order) is positive and s(w) := −w otherwise; two unit simple n-vectors orienting the same n-plane are equal up to sign, so s(η_x) depends only on T_yY. Define ζ(y) := s(η_x) for any x ∈ F_y (y ∈ Y ∖ E), and ζ := 0 elsewhere. ζ is Hⁿ-measurable: on Y_k ∖ E, ζ = s∘η∘(f|A_k)⁻¹ with (f|A_k)⁻¹ continuous (5.2), s Borel, and η agreeing with a Borel function off an Hⁿ-null subset of A_k, whose image is Hⁿ-null (P3(i)); and Y ∖ E ⊆ ⋃_kY_k. Hence (printed 3.7) η_x = ε_xζ(y) with ε_x ∈ {1,−1} for every x ∈ F_y, and (printed 3.8)
 Σ_{x∈F_y}θ(x)η_x = c(y)ζ(y),  c(y) := Σ_{x∈F_y}ε_xθ(x) ∈ ℤ,  |c(y)| ≤ Σ_{x∈F_y}θ(x),  |c(y)| ≡ Σ_{x∈F_y}θ(x) (mod 2).
 c is Hⁿ-measurable on Y ∖ E: c(y) = ⟨Σ_kΣ_{x∈F_y∩A_k}θ(x)η_x, ζ(y)⟩ (Euclidean inner product of n-vectors, |ζ(y)| = 1), and y ↦ 1_{Y_k}(y)(θη)((f|A_k)⁻¹(y)) is Hⁿ-measurable for each k by the same argument.
 5.5 (Printed 3.6.) Let ω ∈ Dⁿ(V) and K := tsupport ω. On M₊, L(x)_#ξ(x) = J^Mf(x)η_x; off M₊ it is 0 (Step 4). The function h := θ⟨ω∘f, η⟩ on M₊ satisfies |h|J^Mf ≤ ‖ω‖θJ^Mf1_{K′} Hⁿ-a.e. on M₊ (P2), which is integrable by 5.1(b). By 5.1 (applied to h⁺, h⁻) and 5.4,
 S(ω) = ∫_{M₊}θ⟨ω∘f, η⟩J^Mf dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝ^Q}Σ_{x∈F_y}θ(x)⟨ω(y), η_x⟩ dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{Y∖E}c(y)⟨ω(y), ζ(y)⟩ dHⁿ(y),   (3.6)
 using that Hⁿ-a.e. y with F_y ≠ ∅ lies in Y ∖ E.

6. (The integer multiplicity representation of S.) Let M′ := {y ∈ Y ∖ E : c(y) ≠ 0}, and on M′ put θ′(y) := |c(y)| ∈ {1,2,…} and ξ′(y) := sign(c(y))ζ(y) (off M′ put θ′ := 1, ξ′ := 0). By (3.6), S(ω) = ∫_{M′}θ′⟨ω, ξ′⟩ dHⁿ = `tauAction n M′ θ′ ξ′ ω` for all ω ∈ Dⁿ(V).

7. (Verification of `IsRectifiableTriple V n M′ θ′ ξ′` and integrality — Lemma 3.9.)
 • M′ ⊆ Y ⊆ f(U) ⊆ V.
 • M′ is Hⁿ-measurable (Y is Hⁿ-measurable, E is Hⁿ-null and c is Hⁿ-measurable; 5.1, 5.4), so `NullMeasurableSet M′ μHE[n]`.
 • M′ ⊆ Y is countably n-rectifiable (5.1; `CountablyRectifiable.mono`).
 • θ′ > 0 on M′ and θ′(y) = |c(y)| ∈ ℕ.
 • For compact K ⊆ V: if y ∈ (Y ∖ E) ∩ K then F_y ⊆ K′ = f⁻¹(K) ∩ spt T, so ∫_{M′∩K}θ′ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_KΣ_{x∈M₊∩K′∩f⁻¹(y)}θ(x) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{M₊∩K′}θJ^Mf dHⁿ < ∞ (5.1(b)); hence θ′ is integrable on M′ ∩ K.
 • ξ′ is Hⁿ⌞M′-measurable (ζ and c are), hence a.e. strongly measurable (values in a finite-dimensional space).
 • Orientation: θ′ is positive, integer valued and locally Hⁿ-integrable on the countably n-rectifiable set M′ ⊆ V, so by Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 and Remark 1.8(1) (applied to M′ ∩ V_i for open V_i ⊂⊂ V exhausting V; P4) the weighted approximate tangent space of M′ with respect to θ′ exists at Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M′ and equals the approximate tangent space T_yM′ (Remark 1.8(1): up to an Hⁿ-null set M′ is covered by compact pieces M′_j on which θ′ is continuous, and at Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M′_j the weighted tangent space of (M′,θ′) exists iff T_yM′_j exists, and then they coincide; T_yM′_j = T_yM′ at Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M′_j by P4(a)); by P4(a) applied to M′ ⊆ Y (V₀ := V), T_yM′ = T_yY at Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M′; and ξ′(y) = ±ζ(y) orients T_yY (5.4). Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M′ there is an orthonormal basis τ of the weighted approximate tangent space of (M′, θ′) at y with ξ′(y) = simpleNVector τ or ξ′(y) = −simpleNVector τ.
 Therefore S is integer multiplicity, S = τ(M′, θ′, ξ′). Together with Step 3 this proves `LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity`.

8. (Degenerate dimensions.) If n > P, no orthonormal n-frame exists in ℝ^P, so the orientation property forces Hⁿ(M) = 0, T = 0 and S = 0 (with M′ = ∅). If n > Q then every n-vector of ℝ^Q is 0 (all n-covectors on ℝ^Q vanish), so L(x)_#ξ(x) = 0, J^Mf ≡ 0, M₊ = ∅, S = 0 and M′ = ∅. If n = 0, simple 0-vectors are ±1, J^Mf ≡ 1, M is countable and locally finite in U (θ ≥ 1 is locally H⁰-integrable), S(ω) = Σ_{y} c(y)ω(y) with c(y) = Σ_{x∈f⁻¹(y)∩M} θ(x)ξ(x) ∈ ℤ, and the weighted tangent space at each point of the locally finite set M′ is {0}; Steps 1–7 apply verbatim with these simplifications.
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) = 0 for T = τ(M,θ,ξ) integer multiplicity; locally Lipschitz f maps Hⁿ-null sets to null sets and σ-finite measurable sets to measurable sets; approximate tangent spaces are local (subsets, C¹ manifolds, existence on rectifiable sets).
Decompose M into C¹ pieces; weighted tangent spaces exist a.e. and equal T_xN_j; ξ orients them.
Tangential differential d^Mf_x via C¹ charts and Rademacher; L(x) := d^Mf_x∘π_{T_xM} satisfies the HasDerivAt clause.
Define S(ω) by (3.6); integrability on f⁻¹(spt ω) ∩ spt T (compact) gives S ∈ D_n(V) and IsLipschitzPushforward T f S.
Jacobian and induced orientation η_x (3.4–3.5); area formula: preimages in M₊ of Hⁿ-null image sets are null, Y = f(M₊) is countably n-rectifiable, Hⁿ-measurable and locally Hⁿ-finite in V.

C¹ approximation + inverse function theorem: up to a null set M₊ is a disjoint union of pieces A_k on which f is an injective C¹ immersion into an embedded manifold N′_k with d^Mf_x(T_xM) = T_{f(x)}N′_k.

Tangent agreement: the image complement Y ∖ f(A_k) has zero density a.e. on f(A_k), so T_yY = T_y f(A_k) = T_yN′_k there (overlapping sheets agree); pulling the exceptional image sets back through the area formula gives d^Mf_x(T_xM) = T_yY for every x ∈ f⁻¹(y) ∩ M₊ at Hⁿ-a.e. y.
Measurable orientation ζ(y) of T_yY, finite fibres, integer multiplicity c(y) = Σ_x ±θ(x) (3.7–3.8), and S(ω) = ∫_Y c⟨ω,ζ⟩dHⁿ (3.6).

Verify IsRectifiableTriple for (M′ = {c ≠ 0}, |c|, sign(c)ζ): measurability, rectifiability, local integrability by the area formula, orientation by Ch. 3, 1.9 and locality of tangent spaces; degenerate dimensions n > P, n > Q, n = 0.

subproblems.title: Slicing theorem (Simon §4, 4.4–4.10)
subproblems.statement: For all P, m, open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every T ∈ D_{m+1}(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ and M_W(∂T) < ∞ for all W ⊂⊂ U, and every f : ℝ^P → ℝ which is L-Lipschitz on U, there is a family S_t ∈ D_m(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with: (i) IsSlice T f t S_t, i.e. S_t = ∂(T⌞{f<t}) − (∂T)⌞{f<t}, for every t; (ii) spt S_t ⊆ spt T ∩ {f = t} for every t; (iii) if T is integer multiplicity, S_t is integer multiplicity for L¹-a.e. t; (iv) for every open W ⊆ U, every L_W ≥ 0 with ‖Df‖ ≤ L_W Lebesgue-a.e. on W, every a < b and every R with IsRestriction T {x ∈ U : a < f x < b} R, there is a measurable g : ℝ → [0,∞] with M_W(S_t) ≤ g(t) for all t ∈ (a,b) and ∫_{(a,b)} g ≤ L_W·M_W(R).
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, §4 (pp. 153–158): Lemma 4.1, Remark 4.2, 4.3, Definition 4.4, Lemma 4.5 and its printed proof, the definitions 4.6–4.7, the properties 4.8–4.10 and their printed proof via 4.11 (including the closing sentence “To handle general Lipschitz f we simply use f^{(σ)} in place of f … then let σ ↓ 0”). Book n = m + 1. The printed proofs are copied below in numbered form; the steps the book leaves implicit (the measure representation used for restrictions, the a.e.-independence of exceptional sets, the passage from 4.9 to the measurable majorant required by the Lean statement) are filled in. Errata applied: (i) the right side of 4.10 is printed M(T ⌞ {a < f < b}); the proof (4.9) gives M_W(T ⌞ {a < f < b}), which is what is proved (Lean statement, README); (ii) in 4.9/4.10 the printed constant ess sup_W|Df| is used in the form “any L_W ≥ |Df| Lebesgue-a.e. on W”; (iii) in 4.11 “conclude the first part of 4.11” should read “the first part of 4.9”; (iv) the proof of 4.8–4.9 is printed for ⟨T,f,t₊⟩ (“similarly for t₋”); it is written here for the slice ⟨T,f,t₋⟩ of 4.6, which is the slice of the Lean statement. Correction of the previous draft (R1–R3): the mass measures are now constructed by the Riesz theorem on the locally compact space U (Radon on U, i.e. finite on compact subsets of U only) and then extended by zero to ℝ^P; no finiteness on compact subsets of ℝ^P is asserted (it can fail near ∂U, see R1′), and the representation, uniqueness and restriction statements R1–R3 and all later steps use only these local hypotheses.

Setting. U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ D_{m+1}(U) with M_W(T) < ∞ and M_W(∂T) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U; f : ℝ^P → ℝ with |f(x) − f(y)| ≤ L|x − y| for x, y ∈ U. Write n := m + 1. Notation |α|, ‖ω‖, w^β, |w| and Fact A (w(α) = Σ_β α(e_β)w^β, |w(α)| ≤ |α||w|) as in the conventions (|α| = `covectorEuclideanNorm`). Hⁿ = μHE[n].

Preliminaries (Simon 2.7–2.9 and 2.12 with proofs).
(R0) Mass estimate: |X(ω)| ≤ M_W(X)‖ω‖ whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W (±ω/‖ω‖ is mass-admissible).
(R1) Representation (2.7), constructed on U and extended by zero. Let X ∈ D_k(U) with M_W(X) < ∞ for all W ⊂⊂ U. By R0, X is bounded for ‖·‖ on test forms supported in any W ⊂⊂ U; test forms are ‖·‖-dense in the continuous forms with compact support in W (mollification ω_ε = ϕ_ε*ω keeps |ω_ε| ≤ ‖ω‖ and support in W for small ε), so X extends uniquely to a linear functional X̄ on C_c(U; Λ^k(ℝ^P)) (continuous k-forms on the open set U with compact support in U) which is bounded on each C_c(W; Λ^k), W ⊂⊂ U. Apply the vector-valued Riesz representation theorem on the locally compact Hausdorff space U itself (Simon Ch. 1, 4.14; SimonGMT `simon_theorem_4_14` with the space U and H := Λ^k(ℝ^P) ≅ ℝ^{#I(k,P)} carrying the Euclidean coefficient inner product): there are a Radon measure μ_U on U — a Borel regular measure on U which is finite on every compact subset of U — and a μ_U-measurable ν : U → H with |ν| = 1 μ_U-a.e. and X̄(ω) = ∫_U Σ_β ω(e_β)ν^β dμ_U. Moreover μ_U(W) = sup{X̄(ω) : ω ∈ C_c(W;Λ^k), |ω| ≤ 1} for every open W ⊆ U (the total variation of the vector measure νμ_U on W; “≥” by Cauchy–Schwarz, “≤” by Lusin approximation of ν on compact subsets of W), and by the same mollification this supremum equals the supremum over test forms, i.e. μ_U(W) = M_W(X). (`simon_theorem_4_14` gives ν measurable for the Carathéodory σ-algebra of μ_U; since μ_U is Borel regular and σ-finite — U is σ-compact and μ_U is finite on compact subsets of U — ν agrees μ_U-a.e. with a Borel map, which we use instead, and we use the Borel restriction of μ_U.) Extend by zero: μ_X(A) := μ_U(A ∩ U) for Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P (the push-forward of μ_U under the inclusion U ↪ ℝ^P), X⃗^β := ν^β on U (Fact A) and X⃗ := 0 on ℝ^P ∖ U. Then: μ_X(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0; μ_X(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; μ_X(W) = M_W(X) ∈ [0,∞] for every open W ⊆ U; |X⃗| = 1 μ_X-a.e.; and for every ω ∈ D^k(U) the function x ↦ ⟨ω(x), X⃗(x)⟩ is μ_X-integrable (it is bounded by ‖ω‖ and vanishes off the compact set tsupport ω ⊆ U, on which μ_X is finite) with X(ω) = ∫⟨ω, X⃗⟩dμ_X; that is, `IsMeasureRepresentation X μ_X X⃗`.
(R1′) Warning and bookkeeping. μ_X is in general not a Radon measure on ℝ^P: it may be infinite on compact subsets of ℝ^P which meet ∂U. Example: P = 1, U = (0,1), X(a dx) := ∫_0^1 a(x)x⁻¹dx; X and ∂X (∂X(φ) = ∫_0^1 φ′(x)x⁻¹dx = ∫_0^1 φ(x)x⁻²dx) have locally finite mass in U, but μ_X([0,1]) = ∫_0^1 x⁻¹dx = ∞. Accordingly no finiteness of μ_T or μ_{∂T} beyond compact subsets of U is used anywhere below: every integral that occurs has an integrand vanishing outside the compact support (⊆ U) of a test form, or is a quantity μ_T(W ∩ B) for an open W ⊆ U, which is allowed to be +∞ (all mass bounds are inequalities in [0,∞]); the finiteness of μ_T(K ∩ ·) and μ_{∂T}(K ∩ ·) is used only for compact K ⊆ U.
(R2) Uniqueness. If (μ, v) satisfies `IsMeasureRepresentation X μ v`, then ∫_A v(ω)dμ = ∫_A ⟨ω, X⃗⟩dμ_X for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P and every ω ∈ D^k(U). Proof: (i) for every compact K ⊆ U, testing with χ dx^β (χ ∈ C_c^∞(U), 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K) shows that χv^β is μ-integrable, so v^β ∈ L¹(μ⌞K); hence for every open W ⊂⊂ U the signed measures ν_β := (v^βμ)⌞W and ν′_β := (X⃗^βμ_X)⌞W have finite total variation. (ii) For φ ∈ C_c^∞(W), testing with φ dx^β gives ∫φ dν_β = X(φ dx^β) = ∫φ dν′_β; approximating φ ∈ C_c(W) uniformly by mollifications supported in a fixed compact subset of W (dominated convergence) gives ∫φ dν_β = ∫φ dν′_β for all φ ∈ C_c(W). (iii) Two finite signed Borel measures on the open set W that agree on C_c(W) are equal: the indicator of an open subset of W is an increasing limit of functions in C_c(W) with values in [0,1], so they agree on open subsets of W (dominated convergence), and the Borel sets on which they agree form a Dynkin system containing the π-system of open sets. (iv) Given ω ∈ D^k(U), choose an open W ⊂⊂ U with tsupport ω ⊆ W; for Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫_A v(ω)dμ = Σ_β∫_{A∩W}ω(e_β)dν_β = Σ_β∫_{A∩W}ω(e_β)dν′_β = ∫_A⟨ω, X⃗⟩dμ_X (Fact A; v(ω) = Σ_βω(e_β)v^β vanishes off tsupport ω; the integrands are bounded Borel functions).
(R3) Restriction (2.9). For a Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P define X⌞A(ω) := ∫_A ⟨ω, X⃗⟩dμ_X (absolutely convergent by R1: the integrand vanishes off the compact set tsupport ω ⊆ U, where μ_X is finite). Then X⌞A ∈ D_k(U): it is linear, and if ω_j → ω in D^k(U) with tsupports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U, then ⟨ω_j, X⃗⟩ → ⟨ω, X⃗⟩ uniformly with the dominating function (sup_j‖ω_j‖)1_K, μ_X(K) < ∞, so X⌞A(ω_j) → X⌞A(ω). `IsRestriction X A (X⌞A)` holds (A measurable, representation (μ_X, X⃗) of R1), and any S with `IsRestriction X A S` equals X⌞A (R2). Mass of a restriction: for open W ⊆ U, M_W(X⌞A) = sup{X⌞A(ω) : ω test form, tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1} equals, by the mollification of R1, the supremum of ∫_{A}⟨ω, X⃗⟩dμ_X over continuous ω with compact support in W and |ω| ≤ 1; since |X⃗| = 1 μ_X-a.e. and μ_U⌞A is a Radon measure on U (a Borel measure finite on compact subsets of the σ-compact metric space U), this supremum is μ_U(W ∩ A) (“≤” by Cauchy–Schwarz; “≥” by inner regularity of μ_U⌞A on W and Lusin approximation of X⃗ on compact subsets of W, as in R1). Hence M_W(X⌞A) = μ_X(W ∩ A) ∈ [0,∞] for every open W ⊆ U. More generally for bounded h : ℝ^P → ℝ whose restriction to U is Borel (e.g. h = χ∘f with f continuous on U and χ continuous; the values of h off U are irrelevant because μ_X(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, so h may be replaced by h·1_U), X⌞h(ω) := ∫ h⟨ω, X⃗⟩dμ_X, and if h is smooth on a neighbourhood of tsupport ω then hω is a test form and X⌞h(ω) = X(hω).
(R4) Locality. If X vanishes on an open W ⊆ U (X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W), then μ_X(W) = M_W(X) = 0.
(R5) For a 1-covector α and a k-covector γ, |α∧γ| ≤ |α||γ| (rotate coordinates so that α = |α|dx¹; then α∧γ = |α|dx¹∧γ, and dx¹∧ kills the coefficients of γ containing dx¹ and maps the others isometrically; the Euclidean coefficient norm is invariant under orthogonal changes of coordinates).

Apply R1 to T and to ∂T (both have locally finite mass in U): μ_T, T⃗, μ_{∂T}, ∂T⃗ (Radon on U, extended by zero to ℝ^P; by R1′ only their finiteness on compact subsets of U is used).

Proof.

1. (Definition of the slices, 4.6.) For t ∈ ℝ let A_t := {x ∈ U : f(x) < t}; f is continuous on U and U is open, so A_t is open, in particular Borel. Define S_t(ω) := (T⌞A_t)(dω) − ((∂T)⌞A_t)(ω) for ω ∈ D^m(U). S_t is linear and sequentially continuous (each term is, and d is continuous on test forms), so S_t ∈ D_m(U). With A := T⌞A_t and B := (∂T)⌞A_t, R3 gives `IsRestriction T {x | x ∈ U ∧ f x < t} A` and `IsRestriction T.boundary {…} B`, and S_t(ω) = A.boundary(ω) − B(ω). Hence `IsSlice T f t (S_t)` for every t.

2. (Support, 4.8.) (a) If tsupport ω ⊆ A_t, then tsupport dω ⊆ A_t, so (T⌞A_t)(dω) = T(dω) and ((∂T)⌞A_t)(ω) = ∂T(ω) = T(dω) (the integrands vanish off A_t); hence S_t(ω) = 0. (b) If tsupport ω ⊆ B_t := {x ∈ U : f(x) > t}, then dω and ω vanish on A_t, so both terms are 0. (c) If W ⊆ U is open and T vanishes on W, then ∂T vanishes on W, so μ_T(W) = μ_{∂T}(W) = 0 (R4), and for tsupport ω ⊆ W both integrals defining S_t(ω) vanish. Now let x ∈ U with x ∉ spt T ∩ {f = t}. If f(x) ≠ t, continuity of f on U gives a ball around x with compact closure inside A_t or inside B_t, on which S_t vanishes by (a)/(b). If x ∉ spt T, x lies in one of the open sets W (closure compact ⊆ U) on which T vanishes, and S_t vanishes on W by (c). In both cases x ∈ zeroRegion(S_t). Hence (S_t).support ⊆ T.support ∩ {x | f x = t}.

3. (Pointwise mass bound, 4.9–4.11 with f^{(σ)} in place of f.) Let W ⊆ U be open and L_W ≥ 0 with ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ L_W for Lebesgue-a.e. x ∈ W (`fderiv`; by Rademacher f is differentiable a.e. on U, and the weak and classical derivatives agree). Fix t ∈ ℝ and ω ∈ D^m(U) with tsupport ω =: K ⊆ W and ‖ω‖ ≤ 1. Choose δ₀ > 0 with the closed δ₀-neighbourhood of K inside W. For 0 < σ < δ₀ let f_σ := ϕ_σ * f on the δ₀−σ neighbourhood of K (ϕ_σ a mollifier on ℝ^P; only values of f on W are used). Then f_σ is smooth near K, |f_σ − f| ≤ Lσ on K, and Df_σ(x) = ∫Df(x−y)ϕ_σ(y)dy, so |Df_σ| ≤ L_W on K.
Fix h > 0 and ε > 0 and a smooth nonincreasing χ : ℝ → [0,1] with χ = 1 on (−∞, t−h], χ = 0 on [t, ∞) and |χ′| ≤ (1+ε)/h. The forms χ(f_σ)ω and χ′(f_σ)df_σ∧ω are test forms with tsupport ⊆ K, and (4.11)
∂T(χ(f_σ)ω) = T(d(χ(f_σ)ω)) = T(χ′(f_σ)df_σ∧ω) + T(χ(f_σ)dω).
By R1 and R5, |T(χ′(f_σ)df_σ∧ω)| ≤ ∫|χ′(f_σ)||df_σ||ω| dμ_T ≤ ((1+ε)/h)·L_W·μ_T(K ∩ {t−h < f_σ < t}) ≤ ((1+ε)/h)L_W μ_T(K ∩ {t−h−Lσ < f < t+Lσ}).
As σ ↓ 0, χ(f_σ) → χ(f) uniformly on K, so by dominated convergence (μ_T(K), μ_{∂T}(K) < ∞) ∂T(χ(f_σ)ω) = ∫χ(f_σ)⟨ω,∂T⃗⟩dμ_{∂T} → (∂T)⌞χ(f)(ω) and T(χ(f_σ)dω) → T⌞χ(f)(dω); and μ_T(K ∩ {t−h−Lσ < f < t+Lσ}) ↓ μ_T(K ∩ {t−h ≤ f ≤ t}) (finite measure, decreasing sets). Hence
|(∂T)⌞χ(f)(ω) − T⌞χ(f)(dω)| ≤ ((1+ε)/h)·L_W·μ_T(W ∩ {t−h ≤ f ≤ t}).
Now let h ↓ 0 (with corresponding χ = χ_h): χ_h(f(x)) → 1_{A_t}(x) for every x ∈ U (if f(x) < t then χ_h(f(x)) = 1 once h < t − f(x); if f(x) ≥ t it is 0), so by dominated convergence the left side tends to |((∂T)⌞A_t)(ω) − (T⌞A_t)(dω)| = |S_t(ω)|. Therefore |S_t(ω)| ≤ (1+ε)·L_W·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_T(W ∩ {t−h ≤ f ≤ t}), where the product is 0 if L_W = 0 (each approximant is then 0, the measures involved being finite). Letting ε ↓ 0 and taking the supremum over admissible ω:
(4.9) M_W(S_t) ≤ L_W·Λ(t) for every t ∈ ℝ, Λ(t) := liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ μ_T(W ∩ {t−h ≤ f ≤ t}) ∈ [0,∞]   (with 0·∞ := 0).

4. (Integral bound 4.10 with a measurable majorant.) Fix a < b and R with `IsRestriction T {x | x ∈ U ∧ a < f x ∧ f x < b} R`. By R3, R = T⌞{a < f < b} and M_W(R) = μ_T(W ∩ {a < f < b}) =: Q.
 • If L_W = 0: take g ≡ 0. By (4.9), M_W(S_t) = 0 ≤ g(t), and ∫⁻ g = 0.
 • If L_W > 0 and Q = ∞: take g ≡ ∞; then M_W(S_t) ≤ g(t) and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g ≤ ∞ = L_W·Q.
 • If L_W > 0 and Q < ∞: let G(s) := μ_T(W ∩ {a < f ≤ s}) (G = 0 for s ≤ a, nondecreasing, G(s) ≤ Q < ∞ for s < b, and right-continuous on (−∞, b) by continuity from above of the measure μ_T⌞W on sets of finite measure; only right-continuity at points < b is used below — for s ≥ b, G may be +∞ when W is not relatively compact in U). For t ∈ (a,b) and small h > 0 (t−h−h² > a), {t−h ≤ f ≤ t} ⊆ {t−h−h² < f ≤ t}, so h⁻¹μ_T(W ∩ {t−h ≤ f ≤ t}) ≤ (1+h)·(G(t) − G(t−k))/k with k := h + h² (h⁻¹ = (1+h)/k); since h ↦ h + h² is an increasing bijection near 0 and 1+h → 1, Λ(t) ≤ D(t) := liminf_{k↓0}(G(t) − G(t−k))/k. Define g(t) := L_W·D(t) for t ∈ (a,b) and g(t) := 0 otherwise. Measurability: for fixed t, k ↦ G(t) − G(t−k) is left-continuous (right-continuity of G), so the infimum over k ∈ (0,1/j) equals the infimum over rational k ∈ (0,1/j); each t ↦ (G(t)−G(t−k))/k is Borel (G monotone), so D = lim_j inf_{k∈ℚ∩(0,1/j)} (…) is Borel. By (4.9), M_W(S_t) ≤ L_W Λ(t) ≤ g(t) for all t ∈ (a,b). By Lebesgue's theorem for monotone functions, G is differentiable a.e. with G′ = D a.e. and ∫_{[a′,b′]} G′ ≤ G(b′) − G(a′) for a < a′ < b′ < b; by monotone convergence ∫_{(a,b)} D ≤ G(b−) − G(a) ≤ μ_T(W ∩ {a < f < b}) = Q. Hence ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g ≤ L_W·Q = L_W·M_W(R).
This proves the last conjunct of `SlicingTheorem` (the printed 4.10 is the upper-integral form of exactly this).

5. (Slicing of rectifiable sets, Lemma 4.1 and Remark 4.2. The Ch. 3 results used below (1.6, 1.8, 1.9, 2.10, co-area) are applied on M ∩ U_i for open U_i ⊂⊂ U exhausting U, since θ is integrable only on compact subsets of U; weighted tangent spaces are local.) Assume now T = τ(M, θ, ξ) is integer multiplicity (n = m+1, `IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ`, θ ∈ {1,2,…} on M). By McShane extension (`LipschitzOnWith.extend_real`) we may replace f by an L-Lipschitz function on ℝ^P agreeing with f on U; nothing below depends on f off U (M ⊆ U and all sets are intersected with U). Let ∇^Mf be the tangential gradient (Simon Ch. 3, 2.1; defined Hⁿ-a.e. on M via the C¹ decomposition M = ⋃M_j, M_j ⊆ N_j, Hⁿ(M₀) = 0), M₊ := {x ∈ M : ∇^Mf(x) ≠ 0}, M_t := f⁻¹(t) ∩ M₊. Lemma 4.1 (printed proof: (1) is Ch. 3, 2.10(2); (2) follows from Ch. 3, 1.6 together with ∇^Mf(x) ∈ T_xM and ⟨∇^Mf(x), τ⟩ = 0 for τ ∈ T_xM_t; the last part is the co-area formula of Ch. 3, §2): for L¹-a.e. t, M_t is countably (n−1)-rectifiable and Hⁿ⁻¹-measurable, and for Hⁿ⁻¹-a.e. x ∈ M_t both T_xM_t and T_xM exist, T_xM_t ⊆ T_xM is (n−1)-dimensional and T_xM = T_xM_t ⊕ ℝ∇^Mf(x); and for every nonnegative Hⁿ-measurable g on M, ∫_{−∞}^{∞}∫_{M_t} g dHⁿ⁻¹ dt = ∫_M |∇^Mf| g dHⁿ. Remark 4.2: applying this to g·1_{f<s} gives that s ↦ ∫_{M∩{f<s}}|∇^Mf|g dHⁿ is absolutely continuous with derivative ∫_{M_s} g dHⁿ⁻¹ for L¹-a.e. s (for integrable signed g as well, by splitting g = g⁺ − g⁻).

6. (The integer multiplicity slice, 4.3–4.4.) For the L¹-a.e. t of Step 5, define for x ∈ M_t: ξ_t(x) := ξ(x) ⌞ (∇^Mf(x)/|∇^Mf(x)|) (interior product: ⟨ξ⌞w, α⟩ = ⟨ξ, w*∧α⟩ for α ∈ Λ^{n−1}), and θ_t := θ|M_t. By 4.3, ξ_t(x) is a unit simple (n−1)-vector orienting T_xM_t for Hⁿ⁻¹-a.e. x ∈ M_t (if ξ = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_n with τ_n = ∇^Mf/|∇^Mf| and τ₁,…,τ_{n−1} an orthonormal basis of T_xM_t, then ξ_t = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_{n−1}, up to the sign (−1)^{n−1}). Define ⟨T,f,t⟩ := τ(M_t, θ_t, ξ_t) (Definition 4.4). It is integer multiplicity for L¹-a.e. t: (i) M_t ⊆ U, Hⁿ⁻¹-measurable, countably (n−1)-rectifiable (Step 5); (ii) θ_t ∈ {1,2,…}; (iii) local integrability: choose compacts K_i ↑ U; by the co-area formula ∫∫_{M_t∩K_i} θ dHⁿ⁻¹dt = ∫_{M∩K_i}|∇^Mf|θ dHⁿ ≤ L∫_{M∩K_i}θ dHⁿ < ∞, so for a.e. t every ∫_{M_t∩K_i}θ < ∞, hence θ_t is integrable on M_t ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U; (iv) measurability of ξ_t on M_t for a.e. t (restrictions of Hⁿ-measurable functions on M to the slices M_t are Hⁿ⁻¹-measurable for a.e. t, by the co-area formula applied to indicator functions of the null sets where the measurable modifications differ); (v) orientation: the properties “T_xM exists and ξ(x) = ±(orthonormal frame of T_xM)” hold outside an Hⁿ-null set Z ⊆ M; by the co-area formula ∫Hⁿ⁻¹(Z ∩ M_t)dt = ∫_Z|∇^Mf|dHⁿ = 0, so for a.e. t they hold Hⁿ⁻¹-a.e. on M_t, and then 4.3 applies Hⁿ⁻¹-a.e. on M_t. θ_t is a positive integer-valued locally integrable function on the countably (n−1)-rectifiable M_t, so by Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 and Remark 1.8(1) the weighted approximate tangent space of (M_t, θ_t) exists Hⁿ⁻¹-a.e. on M_t and equals T_xM_t, which ξ_t orients. (For n = 1, M_t is countable and locally finite, the weighted tangent space at each point is {0}, and ξ_t = ±1.)

7. (Lemma 4.5(2): the integer multiplicity slice equals S_t for a.e. t.) The printed proof: First (1): for a Lipschitz h on ℝ^P with mollifications h^{(σ)} and any bounded Hⁿ-measurable vector field v with compact support in U, ∫_Mθ v·∇^Mh^{(σ)}dHⁿ → ∫_Mθ v·∇^Mh dHⁿ as σ ↓ 0 (the printed “weak convergence in L²(μ_T)”, localized since μ_T is only locally finite) (check it on each N_j with v vanishing off M_j: in C¹ charts, h^{(σ)} → h uniformly with uniformly bounded gradients, so the tangential gradients converge weakly-* in L^∞; approximate v by continuous fields). Fix t, ε > 0 and let ψ(s) := 1 for s < t−ε, ψ linear on [t−ε, t], ψ(s) := 0 for s > t, and h := ψ∘f. For ω ∈ D^m(U):
(2) (∂T)⌞h(ω) = lim_{σ↓0} ∂T(h^{(σ)}ω) = lim_{σ↓0}[T(dh^{(σ)}∧ω) + T(h^{(σ)}dω)] = lim_{σ↓0}T(dh^{(σ)}∧ω) + T⌞h(dω)
(using R1 for T and ∂T and dominated convergence). Since ξ(x) orients T_xM, ⟨ξ, dh^{(σ)}∧ω⟩ = ⟨ξ ⌞ ∇^Mh^{(σ)}, ω⟩, so by (1)
(3) lim_{σ↓0}T(dh^{(σ)}∧ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ξ⌞∇^Mh, ω⟩ dHⁿ.
By the chain rule (4) ∇^Mh = ψ′(f)∇^Mf Hⁿ-a.e. on M (with ψ′(f) := 0 at the values t, t−ε; ∇^Mf = 0 Hⁿ-a.e. on each level set {f = c} ∩ M). Hence
(∂T)⌞h(ω) = −ε⁻¹∫_{M∩{t−ε<f<t}} θ⟨ξ⌞∇^Mf, ω⟩dHⁿ + T⌞h(dω).
Now let ε ↓ 0. By Remark 4.2 applied to g := θ⟨ξ⌞(∇^Mf/|∇^Mf|), ω⟩1_{M₊} (integrable on M ∩ tsupport ω), for L¹-a.e. t the first term tends to −∫_{M_t}θ⟨ξ_t, ω⟩dHⁿ⁻¹ = −⟨T,f,t⟩(ω); and h = h_ε → 1_{A_t} pointwise on U, so (∂T)⌞h(ω) → ((∂T)⌞A_t)(ω) and T⌞h(dω) → (T⌞A_t)(dω). Hence ⟨T,f,t⟩(ω) = (T⌞A_t)(dω) − ((∂T)⌞A_t)(ω) = S_t(ω) for all t outside an L¹-null set F_ω. To make the null set independent of ω: choose a countable family {ω_k} ⊆ D^m(U) such that every ω ∈ D^m(U) is the limit of some subsequence ω_{k_i} in the C¹ norm with tsupports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U (separability of C¹ on compacts, as in the 2.15 argument). Off F := ⋃_k F_{ω_k} ∪ (the exceptional set of Step 6), both ⟨T,f,t⟩ (a current of locally finite mass, continuous for the C⁰ norm on forms supported in K) and S_t (continuous for the C¹ norm on forms supported in K: by R1, R3, |S_t(ω)| ≤ μ_T(K)‖dω‖ + μ_{∂T}(K)‖ω‖ when tsupport ω ⊆ K, with μ_T(K), μ_{∂T}(K) < ∞ as K ⊆ U is compact) agree on all ω_k, hence on all ω. So for L¹-a.e. t, S_t = ⟨T,f,t⟩ is integer multiplicity (Step 6). This proves the third conjunct of `SlicingTheorem`: if T is integer multiplicity then ∀ᵐ t, `IsIntegerMultiplicity (S t)`.

8. (Conclusion.) The family S : ℝ → D_m(U), S(t) := S_t, satisfies: `IsSlice T f t (S t)` for all t (Step 1); (S t).support ⊆ T.support ∩ {f = t} for all t (Step 2); integer multiplicity for a.e. t when T is (Step 7); and for every open W ⊆ U, every L_W with ‖Df‖ ≤ L_W a.e. on W, every a < b and every R with `IsRestriction T {a < f < b} R`, a measurable g with M_W(S t) ≤ g(t) on (a,b) and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g ≤ L_W·M_W(R) (Steps 3–4). This is `SlicingTheorem`.
proof_key_steps: Riesz representation (2.7) on the locally compact space U, extended by zero to ℝ^P: μ_T, μ_∂T are finite only on compact subsets of U (an example shows the ambient Radon property can fail), and only this local finiteness is used.
Uniqueness of measure representations (finite signed measures on W ⊂⊂ U agreeing on C_c(W)); restrictions (2.9) are unique and M_W(X⌞A) = μ_X(W∩A) ∈ [0,∞].
Define S_t := ∂(T⌞{f<t}) − (∂T)⌞{f<t}; IsSlice holds for every t.
Support: S_t vanishes on {f<t}, on {f>t} and on the zero region of T (4.8).
Mollify f and use 4.11 with cutoffs χ_h (all integrands supported in the compact tsupport ω ⊆ U) to get M_W(S_t) ≤ L_W·liminf_h h⁻¹μ_T(W∩{t−h≤f≤t}) for every t (4.9).
Majorant g := L_W·(lower left Dini derivative of G(s) = μ_T(W∩{a<f≤s})) is Borel; Lebesgue's theorem gives ∫g ≤ L_W M_W(R) (4.10); cases L_W = 0 and infinite mass separately.
For T = τ(M,θ,ξ): co-area slicing of M (4.1–4.2) and the integer multiplicity slice τ(M_t,θ,ξ⌞∇^Mf/|∇^Mf|) (4.3–4.4).
4.5(2): the integer multiplicity slice equals S_t for a.e. t (mollification, chain rule, co-area differentiation, countable dense family of forms).

subproblems.title: Deformation theorem, scaled version (Simon 5.1/5.3)
subproblems.statement: For all m, ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ ≥ 1 there is C = C(m,ℓ) ∈ [0,∞) such that for every T ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^{m+1+ℓ}) with M(T) + M(∂T) < ∞ and every ρ > 0 there are β : 𝓛_{m+1}(ρ) → ℝ, Pc = Σ_F β_F[[F]] (IsLatticeChain ρ β Pc), R ∈ D_{m+2}(ℝ^{m+1+ℓ}) and S ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^{m+1+ℓ}) with T − Pc = ∂R + S, M(Pc) ≤ C M(T), M(∂Pc) ≤ C M(∂T), M(R) ≤ CρM(T), M(S) ≤ CρM(∂T), spt Pc ∪ spt R ⊆ {dist(·, spt T) < 2√(m+1+ℓ)ρ}, spt ∂Pc ∪ spt S ⊆ {dist(·, spt ∂T) < 2√(m+1+ℓ)ρ}; if T is integer multiplicity then every β_F ∈ ℤ and Pc, R are integer multiplicity, and if moreover ∂T is integer multiplicity then S is integer multiplicity.
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 6, §5 (pp. 158–168): statements 5.1 and 5.3, Lemma 5.4 with its printed proof, and the printed “Proof of the Deformation Theorem” (displays (1)–(38)); together with the tools it cites from §§2–4: products with [[(0,1)]] (2.17–2.21), push-forward and homotopy formula (2.23–2.29), 2.35–2.37, 3.2, 3.13, 4.5 and 4.10, and Ch. 2, 2.7–2.9. The printed proof is copied below in numbered form with the details needed for the exact Lean statement filled in. Errata applied: (i) the book's “n, k ∈ {1,2,…}”, “C = C(n,k)”, “L_{k−1}” mean n, ℓ ≥ 1, C(n,ℓ), L_{ℓ−1} (cf. the errata recorded in the docstring of `DeformationTheorem`); (ii) in 5.3 “P = Σ_{F∈𝓛_j(ρ)}” means F ∈ 𝓛_n(ρ), and “if ∂T is integer multiplicity then so is s” means S; (iii) the sign in (20) is corrected (homotopy formula 2.25 with f = id, g = ψ gives X − ψ_#X = −∂h_#([[(0,1)]]×X) − h_#([[(0,1)]]×∂X)); signs of R₁, S₁ are chosen accordingly; (iv) the printed bounds in (11)–(16) are stated as “≤ cM(T)”; the computations give the sharper ≤ cρM(T) (resp. cρ², cσ) used for the Cauchy property; (v) in (23) “<” is replaced by “≤” for the intermediate supports (the final strict bound < 2√(n+ℓ) follows since √n < √(n+ℓ)); (vi) in the selection of the good point a, the measure estimate (5) is replaced by the correct Fubini bound written in Step C2. (vii) The printed estimates (11)–(18) are applied to the pieces T_ρ − T_{ρ/2}, (∂T)_ρ − (∂T)_{ρ/2} for arbitrary ρ; since the Lipschitz push-forward 2.29 requires finite boundary mass, they are stated here only for differences between consecutive “good” radii σ_ν at which the slices of T and of ∂T have finite mass, and the uniform bounds (17)–(18) are obtained by telescoping. Details supplied beyond the printed text in A3 (behind the printed remark “Q, R₁ are integer multiplicity by (19), 4.4, 4.5 and 3.13”): (I) the limit passage identifying the Lipschitz push-forward 2.29 of an integer multiplicity current with the push-forward formula 3.6 fixes a compact target neighbourhood K of spt ω, shows that for all sufficiently small mollification parameters every contributing source point lies (H^k-a.e.) in the compact set g⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X, and dominates all integrands by one integrable function supported there before passing to the limit on each chart piece and summing over the pieces; (II) the identification with the push-forward supplied by the sibling theorem 3.9 compares the two representations of X by Radon–Nikodym uniqueness with respect to λ := H^k⌞(M ∪ M′). The representation X = τ(M′,θ′,ξ′) coming from `IsLipschitzPushforward` (through `IsRectifiableTriple`) has a merely positive, locally integrable real multiplicity θ′, which need not be integer valued or ≥ 1; σ-finiteness of λ is therefore proved from θ′ > 0 and the local integrability of θ′ alone (compact exhaustion K_j and the sets M′ ∩ K_j ∩ {θ′ ≥ 1/r}, each of H^k-measure ≤ r∫_{M′∩K_j}θ′ dH^k < ∞), and Radon–Nikodym uniqueness then gives H^k(M Δ M′) = 0, θ = θ′ and ξ = ξ′ H^k-a.e. on M ∩ M′.

Setting and notation. Book n := m + 1 ≥ 1, ℓ ≥ 1, d := n + ℓ, ambient ℝ^d = `Eucl (m+1+ℓ)`, all currents in U = ℝ^d (`univ`). C = [0,1]^d, q its centre; L_j the j-skeleton of the decomposition ⋃_{z∈ℤ^d}(z + C), 𝓛_j its closed j-faces, 𝓛_j(ρ) = {ρF}; S₁,…,S_N (N = C(d, n+1)) the (n+1)-dimensional coordinate subspaces, p_j the orthogonal projection onto S_j. For a ∈ B_{1/4}(q): L_{ℓ−1}(a) := a + L_{ℓ−1}, d_a(x) := dist(x, L_{ℓ−1}(a)) (1-Lipschitz), L_{ℓ−1}(a;ρ) := {d_a < ρ}. Since a has all coordinates in (1/4,3/4), every point of L_{ℓ−1}(a) has at least n+1 coordinates in a_i + ℤ and every point of L_n at least ℓ integer coordinates, so dist(L_{ℓ−1}(a), L_n) ≥ 1/4. Also (Simon (2)): L_{ℓ−1}(a) = ⋃_{j=1}^N ⋃_{z∈ℤ^d}(z + p_j⁻¹(p_j(a))), hence L_{ℓ−1}(a;ρ) = ⋃_j ⋃_{z∈ℤ^d∩S_j} p_j⁻¹(B_ρ(p_j(a)+z)) (balls in S_j). Conventions (stated here so that this proof is self-contained). For an ambient dimension D, e₁,…,e_D is the standard basis of ℝ^D, I(k,D) the set of strictly increasing multi-indices γ = (γ₁ < ⋯ < γ_k) in {1,…,D}, e_γ := (e_{γ₁},…,e_{γ_k}) and dx^γ := dx^{γ₁}∧⋯∧dx^{γ_k}. For a k-covector α (`Covector (Eucl D) k`), |α| := (Σ_γ α(e_γ)²)^{1/2} (`covectorEuclideanNorm`); for a k-form ω, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|; for a k-vector w (`NVector (Eucl D) k`, a linear functional on k-covectors), ⟨α, w⟩ := w(α), w^γ := w(dx^γ) and |w| := (Σ_γ (w^γ)²)^{1/2}; ‖A‖ is the operator norm of a linear map A. Coordinate fact: every k-covector satisfies α = Σ_γ α(e_γ)dx^γ (an alternating k-linear map is determined by its values on increasing tuples of basis vectors, and dx^γ(e_δ) = δ_{γδ}); hence w(α) = Σ_γ α(e_γ)w^γ and |w(α)| ≤ |α|·|w| (Cauchy–Schwarz). Push-forward of k-vectors: for a linear map A : ℝ^D → ℝ^{D′}, A_# = Λ_kA := `nVectorPushforward k A` is characterized by ⟨α, A_#w⟩ = ⟨A^#α, w⟩ with A^#α := α(A·,…,A·) (Simon 1.8–1.9); it is linear and A_#(simpleNVector τ) = simpleNVector(Aτ₁,…,Aτ_k) (Simon 1.10; SimonGMT `nVectorPushforward_simple`). Unit fact: if τ₁,…,τ_k ∈ ℝ^D are orthonormal then |simpleNVector τ| = 1, because its coordinates (simpleNVector τ)^γ = det(τ_i·e_{γ_j}) are the k×k minors of the D×k matrix with columns τ₁,…,τ_k and, by the Cauchy–Binet formula, Σ_γ det(τ_i·e_{γ_j})² = det(τ_i·τ_j) = 1; consequently, whenever `IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ` holds, |ξ| = 1 H^k-a.e. on M (orientation clause). Mass M = `mass`, spt = `support`.

Part A — tools (Simon §§2–4, Ch. 2).

A1 (Representation, restriction; 2.7–2.9, 2.12). Every X ∈ D_k(ℝ^d) with locally finite mass is X(ω) = ∫⟨ω, X⃗⟩dμ_X with μ_X Radon, |X⃗| = 1 μ_X-a.e., μ_X(W) = M_W(X) for open W (vector Riesz theorem, Ch. 1, 4.14, applied to the ‖·‖-continuous extension of X to continuous compactly supported forms; mollification shows the sup over continuous and over smooth forms agree). Any `IsMeasureRepresentation` of X defines the same vector measure (both agree on continuous compactly supported forms). At H^k-a.e. x ∈ M we have x ∈ spt X by (b), and either x ∈ spt g_ε^#ω (then ζ(x) = 1) or the integrand vanishes; so (g_ε)_#X(ω) = ∫_MF_ε dH^k.

Write M = M₀ ∪ ⋃_{j≥1}M_j (disjoint, H^k-measurable), H^k(M₀) = 0, M_j ⊆ N_j embedded k-dimensional C¹ submanifolds (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3, which use the C¹ approximation theorem Ch. 2, 1.5; embedded C¹ submanifolds are locally closed, hence Borel). Each point of N_j has a graph chart Φ : Ω → N_j, Ω ⊆ ℝ^k an open ball, Φ(w) = x₀ + Q(w, h(w)) with Q orthogonal and h C¹ with ‖Dh‖ ≤ 1 on Ω; then |DΦ(w)v| ≥ |v|, ‖DΦ‖ ≤ 2 and the Jacobian satisfies JΦ = det(DΦᵀDΦ)^{1/2} ≥ 1.
